body.claim: A C# file-scoped namespace contributes no segment to a symbol path, so every type in a C# 10 file is recorded unqualified.
body.detail: namespace Acme.Widgets; yields csharp://Builder where the braced form yields csharp://Acme.Widgets/Builder, because codedoc-lang does not treat file_scoped_namespace_declaration as a naming declaration. Two types of the same name in different namespaces therefore share a symbol path, and a file migrating between the two forms detaches every record in it — measured on serilog, where the migration detached all 163 namespace anchors and left survival at 32.8%. The file-scoped form has been the default project template since C# 10, so this is most C# written since 2021. The fix belongs in codedoc-lang; crates/codedoc-anchor/tests/csharp_namespaces.rs holds an ignored test that will pass once it lands.

body.claim: Corrective words are matched as whole words, never as prefixes, and the list is deliberately short.
body.detail: fixture is not fix and prefix is not fix. A false positive promotes a declaration that did not earn its place, and the whole value of gaps is that the list is short enough to act on, so precision is worth more here than recall. The list is English only; that is a known limit, not an oversight.
